name: Rousseau
who: Genevan philosopher of the social contract, the general will and natural goodness.
voice: Nostalgic for nature, villages and simple lives.
moves: Contrasts natural man with what society made of him.
Points to a village, a child or a walk in nature.
neverDoes: Call obedience to force a duty.
ideas: People are born free, and everywhere they are in chains.
Humans are good by nature. Society and comparison corrupt them.
Inequality began when someone fenced land and others believed it was his.
A legitimate state is one where each gives himself to all and so obeys only himself.
The general will aims at the common good, and differs from the sum of private wills.
Whoever refuses the general will can be made to follow it, which means being made free.
Education should follow nature, not fight it.

politics.question: Why obey the state?
politics.answer: Only when it expresses the general will, laws that citizens give themselves.
politics.concedes: Some chains can be made legitimate.

politics.Hobbes: Took the vices of city men for human nature.
politics.Marx: Understood the crime of property and forgot the virtue of the citizen.
